chunks: From him, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from 'Ammar ibn Marwan, from Sama'ah, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding His saying: 'The fasting person has the choice until the sun declines,' he (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, that is for the obligatory fast, and as for the voluntary fast, he has the right to break his fast at any time he wishes until sunset.'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between breaking an obligatory fast and a voluntary fast according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between the legal flexibility of voluntary (nafl) fasting and the stricter constraints of obligatory (fard) fasting. While the Quranic verse 2:184 grants the choice to break the fast until solar decline for the obligatory Ramadan fast, the Imam clarifies that for voluntary fasts, one may break the fast at any moment before sunset without penalty. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that voluntary acts of worship carry greater leniency, encouraging believers to maintain consistency in nafl fasting without the fear of invalidating the act prematurely.
